current_responsibility: Independently review the Ledger V2 cutover candidate and block release unless every inherited gate is satisfied
settled_decisions: Assign UUIDv7 ledger identifiers at ingest and retain the legacy invoice identifier as external_ref
Use the append-only outbox backfill; dual writes are rejected because replay is not proven idempotent
Cut over through shadow reads followed by tenant cohorts rather than a big-bang switch
Rollback disables Ledger V2 reads and preserves all Ledger V2 rows
active_commitments: Do not enable Ledger V2 reads for a tenant until row count, cent total, and checksum all match
Retain invoice audit records for seven years
Keep Ledger V2 p95 read latency within 15 milliseconds of the legacy path
Stop rollout when the reconciliation mismatch rate exceeds 0.01 percent
Publish the reconciliation report before release approval
hard_constraints: The reviewer must not execute production writes
No schema changes are permitted during release review
Customer PII must remain in the local approved environment
unresolved_work: Prove the retry worker cannot duplicate outbox rows after a crash
Finalize the reconciliation checksum formula for partial refunds
Resolve missing timezone mappings for tenants amber-grove and cedar-labs
Run the representative load test against the release candidate
Add cache invalidation ordering to the rollback runbook
uncertainties: Whether observed duplicate rows came from the retry worker or pre-existing source data
Whether the synthetic latency result predicts tenant-cohort performance
Whether either missing timezone mapping changes invoice-day grouping

new_inferences: The proposed cohort skips the required shadow-read interval.
Row counts alone do not satisfy the reconciliation gate; excluding partial refunds leaves the checksum work unresolved.
The retry-worker duplicate observation cannot be accepted as low risk while crash-retry idempotency remains unproved.
A temporary Redis identifier map does not resolve the missing timezone mappings and conflicts with the superseded canonical-map direction.
Deferring the representative load test leaves the release candidate's latency commitment unverified.
Deleting Ledger V2 rows on rollback contradicts the rollback decision and the prohibition on destructive SQL; delayed cache invalidation leaves a runbook gap.

blocking_findings.rationale: The proposed 25 percent cohort would enable reads without the required shadow-read interval.
Cent totals and checksums are missing, partial refunds are excluded, and the reconciliation report cannot be completed on that basis.
The observed duplicate rows remain unexplained and crash-retry safety has not been proved.
The missing mappings remain unresolved; a Redis identifier map does not establish invoice-day grouping.
The representative load test is pending, so the candidate has not demonstrated the p95 latency commitment.
Deleting Ledger V2 rows conflicts with the prescribed rollback and the prohibition on destructive SQL; cache invalidation ordering remains unresolved.
